info.name: 48Date Backend API
info.description:
# 48Date Backend API

REST API for the **48Date** dating app — NestJS 11 (ESM) · PostgreSQL 16 + Prisma 7 · Redis 7 · JWT.

---

## How this collection is organised

Two root folders:

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| **USER** | All **54 implemented endpoints**, consumed by the Flutter app. Serialised `A-01` → `SS-06`. |
| **ADMIN** | **Empty placeholder.** No admin endpoints exist in the codebase yet — see that folder's description for the verified details. |

### Reading the serials

Each folder has its own letter prefix, and requests are numbered **01..n within that folder** in integration order:

| Folder | Prefix | Count |
|---|---|---|
| 01 · Auth | `A` | 9 |
| 02 · Profile & Media | `P` | 5 |
| 03 · Discovery | `D` | 5 |
| 04 · Matches | `M` | 2 |
| 05 · Chat (REST) | `C` | 2 |
| 06 · Games | `G` | 4 |
| 07 · Dates | `DT` | 11 |
| 08 · Trust Score | `T` | 2 |
| 09 · Safety | `S` | 5 |
| 10 · Subscriptions | `SB` | 3 |
| 11 · Success Stories | `SS` | 6 |

The **folders themselves** are numbered `01` → `11` in the order you should integrate them: finish Auth before Profile, Profile before Discovery, and so on. Within a folder, a lower number is either a dependency of, or independent from, what follows — so `A-01` has no prerequisites at all, while `SS-06` assumes most of the collection already works.

Cross-references in request descriptions use these serials, so "run after **A-03**" always points at exactly one request.

---

## Setup

1. Start the API: `docker compose up -d postgres redis && npm run start:dev`
2. Set the `baseUrl` variable if you are not on `http://localhost:3000`.
3. Run **A-01 Register** → **A-02 Verify OTP** → you are authenticated.

**Dev OTP is always `123456`.**

### Variables are captured for you

Every request that returns an id writes it into a collection variable, so the folders are runnable top-to-bottom without hand-editing anything:

`phone` · `email` · `username` · `accessToken` · `refreshToken` · `resetToken` · `userId` · `imageUrl` · `targetUserId` · `matchId` · `conversationId` · `gameId` · `questionId` · `sessionId` · `datePlanId` · `storyId` · `commentId`

Authentication is set **collection-wide** to `Bearer {{accessToken}}`; public endpoints individually override it to *No Auth*.

> **Re-running A-01:** `phone`, `email` and `username` are generated once and then **persist** in the collection. Since all three are unique in the database, running **A-01 Register** a second time returns `409 Conflict`. To create another fresh account, clear those three variables (and `accessToken`) first — the pre-request script regenerates them.

---

## Response envelope

Every endpoint — success or failure — returns the same shape:

```json
{ "success": true, "message": "Operation successful", "messages": [], "data": { } }
```

```json
{ "success": false, "message": "Validation failed", "messages": ["phone must be ..."], "statusCode": 400 }
```

`messages` carries the full list of validation errors; `message` is the first one, suitable for a toast.

---

## Chat is WebSocket-only for sending

The two REST endpoints in folder **05** only *read*. Sending happens over Socket.IO on the same origin as `baseUrl`, authenticated by passing the JWT in the handshake.

| Direction | Event | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| → emit | `joinRoom` | `{ conversationId }` |
| → emit | `sendMessage` | `{ conversationId, content, type? }` — type = TEXT \| IMAGE \| DATE_INVITE \| SYSTEM |
| → emit | `typing` | `{ conversationId, isTyping }` |
| ← listen | `newMessage` | the saved message |
| ← listen | `typing` | `{ userId, isTyping }` |

Postman's WebSocket request type can drive these, but it is not part of this collection.

---

## Known gaps

Behaviour verified against the running server — worth knowing before you integrate:

- **No admin API at all.** See the ADMIN folder.
- **`POST /auth/request-otp` and `GET /auth/me` do not exist** despite older docs listing them. Registration and login already return tokens and the user object, and `GET /users/profile` (**P-03**) replaces `/auth/me`.
- **Google login does not verify the token signature** — it only base64-decodes the payload.
- **Mapbox place search returns `[]`** unless `MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN` is set.
- **The RevenueCat webhook skips auth entirely** when `REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset.
- Twilio / SMTP / FCM / R2 all **fall back to console logging or local disk** when their env vars are absent, so flows succeed locally without any third-party account.

exec: // Generate a unique phone + email on first run so A-01 Register doesn't collide
// with an account from a previous run. Clear these variables to start fresh.

item.name: USER
item.description:
Everything the Flutter user app consumes — **all 54 implemented endpoints** live here.

Serials run **A-01 → SS-06 in integration order**: each folder assumes the ones above it already work. Follow them top to bottom and the collection is runnable end to end without editing variables by hand, because each request captures the ids the next one needs.

Hard dependencies worth knowing:
- Everything after **A-03** needs an `accessToken`.
- Folders **05, 06, 07** all need a `matchId` from **D-05** / **M-01**, which needs two users who liked each other.
- **DT-10** (rating) requires the date to be `COMPLETED` via **DT-09**.

---

## Getting to a match (needed for folders 04–07)

A match needs **two accounts that both liked each other**, so a single run of this collection cannot produce one. With one fresh account, 27 of the 54 requests pass; the rest correctly return 404/400 because the match-dependent ids do not exist yet.

To get a real `matchId`:

1. Run **A-01 → A-02** once. Note the generated `phone` and the `userId` — call this **User A**.
2. Clear the `phone`, `email`, `accessToken` and `userId` collection variables, then run **A-01 → A-02** again. This is **User B**.
3. As User B, run **D-05 Swipe** with `targetUserId` set to User A's id and `action: LIKE`.
4. Log back in as User A (**A-03** with A's phone), then run **D-05** with `targetUserId` = User B's id and `action: LIKE`.
5. The second like returns `isMatch: true` and captures `matchId` automatically. Folders **04–07** are now runnable.

The id variables ship with the value `REPLACE_ME` so that an unset id fails loudly with a clear 404 rather than silently collapsing to a different route.

item.name: 01 · Auth
item.description:
Account creation, OTP verification, login, token lifecycle and password reset.

**Start here.** A-01 → A-02 → A-03 gets you an `accessToken`, which every other folder depends on. Tokens are captured into collection variables automatically.

OTP in development is always the dummy code `123456` (see `DUMMY_OTP` in `auth.service.ts`). Real Twilio Verify is used only when `TWILIO_*` env vars are set.

request.description:
**Creates an account and returns tokens immediately.**

Auth: public.

Only `phone` (E.164) and `password` (min 8 chars) are enforced as required; every profile field is optional at the API level and can be filled later via `P-02 Profile setup`.

If the phone is not yet verified the response carries `requiresOtp: true` — continue to **A-02**.

Enum values: `gender`/`interestedIn` = MALE | FEMALE | NON_BINARY | OTHER · `smoker`/`alcohol` = NEVER | SOMETIMES | OFTEN | DAILY · `kids` = HAS_KIDS | DOESNT_HAVE_KIDS | PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY · `lookingFor` = LONG_TERM | SHORT_TERM | FRIENDSHIP | CASUAL | STILL_FIGURING_OUT.

**Verifies the signup OTP and flips `isPhoneVerified` / `isEmailVerified`.**

Auth: public. Run after **A-01**.

Dev OTP is always `123456`. `channel` may be `phone` or `email`; send the matching `phone` or `email` field. Returns a fresh token pair.

**Phone/email + password → tokens.**

Auth: public.

If the account is not yet phone-verified the response is `requiresOtp: true` with an OTP instead of tokens — run **A-02** first.

This is the request to re-run whenever your `accessToken` expires.

**Signs in (or auto-creates an account) from a Google ID token.**

Auth: public.

⚠️ The backend currently only base64-decodes the token payload to read `email`/`name` — it does **not** verify the Google signature (`auth.service.ts` `googleLogin`). Any well-formed JWT-shaped string will be accepted. Do not ship this to production as-is.

exec: // Placeholder token: this request only passes once you paste a real Google ID token.
pm.test('SKIPPED - paste a real Google ID token into the body to run this', () => true);

request.description:
**Exchanges a refresh token for a new access/refresh pair.**

Auth: public (the refresh token itself is the credential). Uses `JWT_REFRESH_SECRET`.

The stored `{{refreshToken}}` is sent automatically and the new pair is captured back into collection variables.

**Logs out.**

Auth: Bearer.

Stateless — the server keeps no token denylist, so this simply signals the client to discard its tokens.

**Starts password reset — returns the dummy reset OTP.**

Auth: public.

Always returns success and the dummy OTP `123456` regardless of whether the account exists (deliberate, to prevent account enumeration).

**Verifies the reset OTP and issues a short-lived `resetToken` (15 min).**

Auth: public. Run after **A-07**.

The returned `resetToken` is captured into `{{resetToken}}` for **A-09**.

**Sets a new password using the `resetToken`.**

Auth: public (the reset token is the credential). Run after **A-08**.

`newPassword` must be at least 8 characters. Note this changes the account password — update the `password` collection variable if you change it to something other than the default.

item.name: 02 · Profile & Media
item.description:
Photo upload, profile completion and selfie (face) verification.

Run **P-01** first so you have real image URLs to pass into **P-02**. A profile must be reasonably complete before `isUserVerified` can flip in **P-04**.

request.description:
**Uploads 1–6 images and returns their URLs.**

Auth: Bearer. `multipart/form-data`, field name `files` (any field name works — the controller uses `AnyFilesInterceptor`).

Storage: Cloudflare R2 when all four `R2_*` env vars are set, otherwise falls back to the local `uploads/` directory served at `/uploads/`.

Max 6 files per request. **Pick real files in the Body tab before sending.**

formdata.description: Image file (repeat this key for up to 6 files)

request.description:
**Updates any subset of profile fields.**

Auth: Bearer. Every field is optional — send only what changed.

`images[]` entries need `url` (valid URL) + `isMain` (boolean); 1–6 items. Use URLs returned by **P-01**.

`creativity` / `sports` / `moviesAndDramas` accept only values from the fixed lists in `register.dto.ts` — anything else is rejected by validation.

**Returns the caller's full categorized profile.**

Auth: Bearer.

Response is grouped into `auth`, `basicProfile`, `lifestyle`, `location`, `body`, `interests`, `media`, `meta`. `passwordHash` is never included.

This is the endpoint the Flutter app should call on app-open to hydrate the session.

**Submits a selfie and marks `selfieVerified: true`.**

Auth: Bearer. `multipart/form-data` with a file, **or** JSON `{ "selfieUrl": "https://..." }` for an already-uploaded image.

⚠️ No actual face matching is performed — the service accepts the upload and flips the flag. If the profile is otherwise complete it also sets `isUserVerified: true`.

formdata.description: Alternative to the file: URL of an already-uploaded selfie

request.description:
**Returns the caller's verification flags.**

Auth: Bearer.

Reports `selfieVerified`, `isPhoneVerified`, `isEmailVerified` and the overall `isUserVerified`, plus what is still missing for full verification.

item.name: 03 · Discovery
item.description:
The swipe deck: filter preferences, candidate feed, profile detail and the swipe action.

Set preferences (**D-02**) before fetching the feed (**D-03**) or the deck may come back empty. A `LIKE`/`SUPER_LIKE` that the other user has already sent creates a match — see folder **04**.

request.description:
**Returns the caller's discovery filters.**

Auth: Bearer.

Creates and returns defaults on first call if the user has no `discovery_preferences` row yet.

**Updates age range, distance and preferred gender.**

Auth: Bearer. All fields optional.

Constraints: `minAge`/`maxAge` 18–99, `maxDistanceKm` ≥ 1, `preferredGender` = MALE | FEMALE | NON_BINARY | OTHER.

**Returns the next batch of candidate profiles.**

Auth: Bearer.

Excludes users already swiped, blocked in either direction, and the caller. Filtered by the preferences from **D-02**.

Captures the first candidate id into `{{targetUserId}}` for **D-04** / **D-05**.

exec: } else { console.log('Feed empty — seed more users or widen preferences (D-02).'); }

request.description:
**Full profile of a single candidate.**

Auth: Bearer. Uses `{{targetUserId}}` captured by **D-03**.

Note the route is declared *after* `/discovery/preferences` in the controller so the literal path is not shadowed by this `:id` param.

**Records a LIKE / PASS / SUPER_LIKE.**

Auth: Bearer.

`action` = LIKE | PASS | SUPER_LIKE.

If the target had already liked the caller, a match is created and the response contains `isMatch: true` with the new match — captured into `{{matchId}}`. A SUPER_LIKE also queues a push notification.

item.name: 04 · Matches
item.description:
List and remove mutual matches.

A match is the prerequisite for chat (**05**), games (**06**) and date planning (**07**) — every one of those takes a `matchId`.

request.description:
**All active matches for the caller.**

Auth: Bearer.

Each entry includes the other user's summary profile and the linked `conversationId`. Captures the first `matchId` and `conversationId` into collection variables.

exec: } else { console.log('No matches yet — run D-05 from both sides.'); }

request.description:
**Ends a match.**

Auth: Bearer. Sets the match status to `UNMATCHED`.

⚠️ Destructive for the pair — the conversation becomes inaccessible. Run this last when testing a match-dependent flow.

item.name: 05 · Chat (REST)
item.description:
Conversation list and message history.

**Sending** messages is WebSocket-only — Postman cannot exercise it. See the collection description for the Socket.IO events (`joinRoom`, `sendMessage`, `typing`) and their payloads.

request.description:
**Conversations for the caller, with last message and unread count.**

Auth: Bearer.

One conversation exists per match. Captures the first `conversationId`.

query.description: Rows to skip. Integer, defaults to 0.

request.description:
**Paginated message history for one conversation.**

Auth: Bearer. Caller must be a participant, otherwise 403.

`limit` and `offset` are parsed with `ParseIntPipe` — a non-numeric value returns 400.

item.name: 06 · Games
item.description:
Icebreaker mini-games played inside a match.

Flow: **G-01** to pick a game → **G-02** to open a session for a match → **G-04** to answer each question → **G-03** to poll state. The database is seeded with 4 games / 18 questions by `npm run db:seed`.

request.description:
**All active games with their questions.**

Auth: Bearer.

Captures the first `gameId` and its first `questionId` for **G-02** / **G-04**.

exec: // Capture this question's real optionA: submitAnswer rejects anything
// that isn't an exact match for optionA/optionB.

request.description:
**Opens a game session for a match, or returns the existing in-progress one.**

Auth: Bearer. Idempotent per (match, game).

Both `matchId` and `gameId` must be valid UUIDs and the caller must belong to the match.

**Current state of a session: questions, both players' answers, status.**

Auth: Bearer. Caller must be a participant.

`status` is IN_PROGRESS or COMPLETED.

**Answers one question in the session.**

Auth: Bearer.

`questionId` must be a UUID belonging to the session's game; `selectedOption` must be an **exact, case-sensitive** match for that question's `optionA` or `optionB` — anything else returns 400 with both valid options in the message. `{{selectedOption}}` is captured from **G-01** so this works out of the box. The session flips to COMPLETED once both players have answered everything.

item.name: 07 · Dates
item.description:
The 48-hour date planner: venue search, invitations, the accept/decline/cancel/complete lifecycle, and post-date ratings.

Status machine: `PENDING` → `ACCEPTED` → `COMPLETED`, with `DECLINED` / `CANCELLED` / `NO_SHOW` as terminal branches. Ratings (**DT-10**) are only accepted once a date is `COMPLETED`, and they feed the trust score in folder **08**.

request.description:
**Venue autocomplete via the Mapbox Geocoding API.**

Auth: Bearer.

⚠️ Returns an **empty array** unless `MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN` is set in `.env` — the service logs a warning and degrades silently rather than erroring. Declared before `/dates/:id` so the literal path wins.

**Sends a date invitation to a match.** Creates the plan in `PENDING`.

Auth: Bearer.

Required: `matchId` (UUID), `date` + `startTime` (ISO 8601), `venueName`, `venueAddress`. Optional: `endTime`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `mapboxPlaceId` (from **DT-01**).

query.description: DRAFT | PENDING | ACCEPTED | DECLINED | CANCELLED | COMPLETED | NO_SHOW

request.description:
**All dates where the caller is organiser or invitee.**

Auth: Bearer. All query params optional.

Captures the first `datePlanId` so the rest of this folder is runnable without editing variables.

**Full detail of one date plan.**

Auth: Bearer. 403 unless the caller is organiser or invitee.

**Reschedules or edits a date plan.**

Auth: Bearer. All fields optional — send only what changed.

Typically restricted to the organiser and to plans not yet `COMPLETED` / `CANCELLED`.

**Invitee accepts.** `PENDING` → `ACCEPTED`.

Auth: Bearer — must be the **invitee**, not the organiser.

**Invitee declines.** `PENDING` → `DECLINED` (terminal).

Auth: Bearer — must be the invitee.

**Either party cancels a PENDING or ACCEPTED date.** → `CANCELLED`.

Auth: Bearer.

`reason` is optional, max 300 characters. A late cancellation can log a negative trust event (see folder **08**).

**Marks an ACCEPTED date as COMPLETED.**

Auth: Bearer.

Required before either party can submit a rating in **DT-10**.

**Rates the other party after a completed date.**

Auth: Bearer. Only valid once the date is `COMPLETED`; one rating per user per date.

All four scores are integers 1–5 and required. `comment` max 500 chars. `isAnonymous` hides the rater's identity from the ratee. Feeds the trust score in folder **08**.

body.raw:
{
  "behaviorScore": 5,
  "punctualityScore": 4,
  "safetyScore": 5,
  "overallScore": 5,
  "comment": "Great conversation, showed up on time.",
  "isAnonymous": false
}

request.description:
**Ratings recorded for a date.**

Auth: Bearer. Caller must be a participant.

Ratings marked `isAnonymous` are returned without the rater's identity.

item.name: 08 · Trust Score
item.description:
The reputation score derived from date ratings, verification status and moderation events.

Read-only for users — there is no endpoint to set a score directly. Values change as a side effect of folders **07** (ratings, cancellations) and **09** (reports).

request.description:
**The caller's current score, badge tier and aggregate stats.**

Auth: Bearer.

Creates a baseline `trust_scores` row on first read if none exists.

**Paginated log of events that moved the score.**

Auth: Bearer.

Event types: PROFILE_VERIFIED, DATE_ATTENDED, POSITIVE_FEEDBACK, GHOSTING, NO_SHOW, LATE_CANCELLATION, ABUSIVE_BEHAVIOR.

item.name: 09 · Safety (Blocks & Reports)
item.description:
User-initiated moderation: blocking and reporting.

Blocking is immediate and symmetric in effect — blocked users disappear from each other's discovery feed (**D-03**). Reports are queued for admin review, but note that **no admin endpoints exist yet** to action them (see the Admin root folder).

request.description:
**Blocks a user.**

Auth: Bearer. The id goes in the path, not the body.

Removes the pair from each other's discovery feed and typically ends any active match.

**Users the caller has blocked.**

Auth: Bearer. Paginated.

**Removes a block.**

Auth: Bearer.

The pair becomes discoverable again; a match ended by the block is not restored.

**Files a safety/moderation report.** Created with status `PENDING`.

Auth: Bearer.

`reportedUserId` must be a UUID. `reason` required, max 100 chars; `description` optional, max 1000. Set `blockUser: true` to block in the same call.

**Reports filed by the caller, with their review status.**

Auth: Bearer.

Status values: PENDING | REVIEWING | RESOLVED | DISMISSED.

item.name: 10 · Subscriptions
item.description:
Premium tiers and RevenueCat integration.

Purchases happen **in the mobile app** through RevenueCat, not through this API — the backend learns about them via the webhook (**SB-03**). `SB-01` is public so the paywall can render before login.

request.description:
**Available subscription tiers.**

Auth: **public** — no token needed.

Static catalogue defined in `subscriptions.service.ts` (WEEKLY / MONTHLY / YEARLY with product ids and feature lists), not read from the database.

**The caller's subscription state and premium flag.**

Auth: Bearer.

Returns the active plan, status (ACTIVE | EXPIRED | CANCELLED) and expiry, or a free-tier result when there is no subscription.

**Server-to-server callback from RevenueCat.** Not called by the mobile or admin client.

Auth: shared secret in the `Authorization` header, checked against `REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

⚠️ When that env var is **unset the check is skipped entirely** and any caller can post events (`subscriptions.service.ts` line ~140). Set it before deploying.

Included here so you can replay events locally.

item.name: 11 · Success Stories
item.description:
Community stories from couples who met on the app, plus likes and comments.

Submissions land in `PENDING` and only appear in the public list once approved — **but there is no admin endpoint to approve them yet**, so a freshly submitted story will not show up in **SS-02**. See the Admin root folder.

request.description:
**Submits a success story for moderation.** Created with status `PENDING`.

Auth: Bearer.

`partnerId` required (UUID). `title` max 120 chars; `story` 20–5000 chars. `images[]` is an array of URL strings (upload via **P-01** first).

**Published success stories.**

Auth: **public** — the controller has no guard on this route.

⚠️ Because there is no guard, `req.user` is always undefined here, so viewer-specific fields such as `isLiked` cannot be personalised even if you send a token.

**One story with its comments.**

Auth: **public** (same caveat as SS-02 — no guard, so no personalised fields).

**Toggles the caller's like.**

Auth: Bearer.

Idempotent toggle — calling twice returns to the original state. The response `isLiked` says which way it went.

**Comments on a published story.**

Auth: Bearer. `content` required, max 500 chars.

**Deletes a comment.**

Auth: Bearer — author only; anyone else gets 403.

There is no admin override, since no admin endpoints exist yet.

item.name: ADMIN
item.description:
# ⚠️ No admin endpoints are implemented yet

This folder is an intentionally empty placeholder so the collection structure is ready when the admin API lands. **Nothing has been stubbed or invented here** — adding fake requests would be worse than an empty folder.

## Verified state of the code (as of this collection)

- `src/modules/admin/admin.module.ts` — the controller, service and providers are all **commented out**; the module exports an empty `@Module({})`.
- `AdminModule` is **not imported** into `app.module.ts`, so Nest never registers it.
- `src/modules/admin/types/admin.types.ts` contains only `export {}`.
- The `@Roles()` decorator (`src/common/decorators/roles.decorator.ts`) and `RolesGuard` (`src/common/guards/roles.guard.ts`) both exist but are **applied to zero controllers** — every guarded route in this API uses the plain `JwtAuthGuard`.
- The `Role` enum does contain `ADMIN`, and users carry a `role` field, so the data model is ready.

All 54 routes the server actually maps are user-facing and live under the **USER** folder.

## What the React admin panel will need

These are the gaps implied by features that already exist on the user side — they are **not implemented**, listed only so the work is visible:

- **Moderation queue** — `reports` rows are created by `S-04` with status PENDING and there is currently no way to review, resolve or dismiss them.
- **Success-story approval** — `SS-01` creates stories with status PENDING, and nothing can move them to PUBLISHED, so the public list `SS-02` can never grow.
- **User administration** — suspend/ban, trust-score override, manual verification.
- **Analytics** — signups, matches, dates completed, subscription revenue.

When those endpoints are built, number them **A-01, A-02, …** inside subfolders here, mirroring the USER convention.
